articles.headline: OFAC Amends Venezuela-Related General License and Issues New FAQ
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced the issuance of an amended Venezuela-related General License (GL) on October 16, 2026. This update modifies existing authorizations concerning transactions involving Venezuela.

In conjunction with the amended GL, OFAC also published a new Frequently Asked Question (FAQ) to provide further guidance and clarity on the scope and application of the updated license. This aims to assist stakeholders in understanding their compliance obligations.
The specific details of the amendments and the new FAQ are available on the Treasury Department's website, and parties involved in Venezuela-related transactions are advised to review them carefully.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Iran-Related Entities and Individuals, Sanctions Cuban Bank, Issues New GLs and FAQs
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced a new round of Iran-related sanctions on October 15, 2026, targeting 16 individuals and 11 entities, adding them to its Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List. These targets include financial institutions, currency exchange firms, and energy and trading companies.

Among the designated entities is Cuba's Banco Internacional de Comercio S.A. (BICSA), which was sanctioned due to its ties with Iran's Karafarin Bank, already under sanctions since 2020. The U.S. also imposed sanctions on the Iraq-based International Development Bank for Investment and Finance, citing its provision of financial services and U.S. dollar access for Iran.

In addition to these designations, OFAC issued new and amended General Licenses (GLs) and Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) to provide guidance on the updated sanctions. Cuban Foreign Minister Bruno Rodriguez criticized the action as 'aggressive,' asserting BICSA is an 'absolutely legitimate bank' with legitimate transactions.

articles.headline: OFAC Removes Venezuela-Related Designation
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced the removal of a Venezuela-related designation on October 14, 2026. This action signifies a change in the sanctions status for a previously designated individual or entity.
Such removals typically occur after a review of the circumstances leading to the initial designation and a determination that the criteria for sanctions no longer apply.
The specific identity of the removed party and the implications of this action are detailed in the official notice published by OFAC.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes Counter Narcotics and Counter Terrorism Designations
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations on October 13, 2026, targeting individuals and entities involved in counter narcotics and counter terrorism activities. These actions aim to disrupt illicit financial networks supporting such operations globally.
These designations underscore the U.S. government's ongoing commitment to combating international drug trafficking and terrorist financing by isolating those involved from the U.S. financial system.
Further details regarding the designated parties and the specific reasons for their inclusion on the sanctions list are available in OFAC's official publication.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues International Criminal Court Designation and General Licenses; Removes Burma-Related Designation
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced a new designation related to the International Criminal Court (ICC) on October 9, 2026. This action is accompanied by the issuance of new General Licenses (GLs) to provide specific authorizations related to the designation.
Concurrently, OFAC also announced the removal of a Burma-related designation. This indicates a change in the sanctions status for a previously identified individual or entity connected to Burma.
These actions reflect the dynamic nature of U.S. sanctions policy, addressing evolving foreign policy and national security concerns while also adjusting existing measures as circumstances change.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues New Russia-Related General License
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced the issuance of a new Russia-related General License (GL) on October 9, 2026. This GL provides specific authorizations for certain transactions that would otherwise be prohibited under the Russia sanctions program.
General Licenses are often issued to clarify the scope of sanctions, mitigate unintended consequences, or facilitate certain humanitarian or other permissible activities.
Parties involved in Russia-related transactions are advised to review the details of this new GL to ensure compliance with U.S. sanctions regulations.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes Iran-Related Designations, Issues New Iran-Related GL, and Amends Russia-Related GL
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations on October 8, 2026, targeting individuals and entities deemed to be supporting the Iranian regime. These actions are part of ongoing efforts to exert economic pressure on Iran.

In conjunction with these designations, OFAC issued a new Iran-related General License (GL) to provide specific authorizations for certain transactions. Additionally, an existing Russia-related General License was amended, indicating adjustments to the scope of permissible activities under the Russia sanctions program.
These simultaneous actions highlight OFAC's active role in managing and adapting sanctions programs in response to evolving geopolitical circumstances and national security priorities.

articles.headline: OFAC Removes and Updates Designations, Publishes Iran-Related Alert and Amended FAQ
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced several updates to its sanctions lists on October 5, 2026, including designations removals and updates. These changes reflect ongoing reviews and adjustments to ensure the accuracy and effectiveness of sanctions programs.

Significantly, OFAC published an Iran-related Alert, warning foreign financial institutions (FFIs) that continue to transact with sanctioned Iranian financial institutions that they 'could be targeted at any time without advance notification.' This alert is part of 'Operation Economic Outcast,' launched in August 2026 to cut off financial resources to the Iranian regime.

Furthermore, OFAC published an amended Iran-related Frequently Asked Question (FAQ 156), which removed language indicating that OFAC would generally contact an FFI before making a finding of sanctionable activity. This change signals a heightened potential for FFIs with exposure to Iranian banks to face U.S. sanctions without prior warning.
articles.source: U.S. Treasury OFAC / Global Sanctions and Export Controls Blog

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes New Counter Terrorism Designations
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new counter terrorism designations on October 2, 2026. These actions target individuals and entities identified as supporting international terrorist organizations.
These designations aim to disrupt the financial and material support networks of terrorist groups, thereby safeguarding U.S. national security interests.
The specific details of the designated parties and the nature of their involvement in terrorism are outlined in OFAC's official release.

articles.headline: Bank of America Settles with OFAC for $11,662,930 in Sanctions Violations
body: Bank of America, N.A. has agreed to a settlement with the U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) for $11,662,930. This settlement resolves the bank's potential civil liability for 475 apparent violations of multiple sanctions programs, including those targeting Iran, Russia, narcotics, and global terrorism.

The apparent violations occurred when Bank of America channeled correspondent banking payments through blocked banks due to technical and human error, allowed designated individuals to make payments and withdraw funds due to poor sanctions alert calibration, failed to promptly update watchlists, and mishandled business accounts associated with blocked persons.

The settlement amount reflects OFAC's determination that the apparent violations were non-egregious and largely not voluntarily self-disclosed. No reduction was applied to the base penalty for remedial measures or cooperation.

articles.headline: Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is easing export controls on certain Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs or drones) and related parts, components, accessories, attachments, technology, and software under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Specifically, this rule: eliminates wind gust tolerance as a parameter for determining UAV controls under the EAR; increases the threshold for national security controls on certain UAVs from an endurance of 30 minutes to an endurance of 3 hours; makes conforming changes to remove national security controls on software and technology associated with UAVs with an endurance less than 3 hours; maintains military end-use and end-user controls on those lower endurance drones and associated software and technology; clarifies Commerce Control List (CCL) controls for certain UAVs specially designed for military use; and removes national security controls on certain specially designed parts, components, accessories, and attachments for such UAVs as they do not provide any significant military or intelligence capabilities.

articles.headline: Implementation of EAR Export Controls on Silencers, Mufflers, and Sound Suppressors; and Other Firearms Related Changes
body: The Department of Commerce (Commerce), Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is revising the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) and the Commerce Control List (CCL) to appropriately control certain silencers, mufflers, and sound suppressors (sound suppressors) that will no longer be described on the International Traffic in Arms Regulations U.S. Munitions List (USML). This interim final rule (IFR) complements a Department of State interim final rule published elsewhere in this issue of the Federal Register (International Traffic in Arms Regulations: USML Category I Firearm Suppressors (1400-AG11) (State IFR)). This transfer of jurisdiction will reduce the regulatory burden on exports of sound suppressors. This IFR also revises the EAR to allow firearms and related items to be temporarily exported and reexported under a license exception as tools of trade, thereby relieving exporters of the regulatory burden of applying for authorization. Finally, this IFR clarifies which items fall within the scope of the EAR's entry clearance requirements for a temporary import.

articles.headline: Enhanced Favorable Treatment for the United Arab Emirates Under the Export Administration Regulations
body: In this final rule, the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) amends the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) to provide enhanced favorable treatment for the United Arab Emirates (UAE). Specifically, BIS is removing the UAE from Country Groups D:3 and D:4 and adding the UAE to Country Group A:5. More license exceptions will now be available, including Strategic Trade Authorization (STA) for the UAE Government and approved commercial entities in the UAE. STA will authorize the export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) of military items; certain commercial satellites and spacecraft; and dual-use items useful in, inter alia, oil and gas production, desalination, and civil nuclear power generation. The UAE Government and approved commercial entities will also have license-free access to advanced computing items, consistent with the May 2025 U.S.-UAE Artificial Intelligence Cooperation framework, without compromising U.S. digital infrastructure buildout.
